To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
suppression of GABA(A)ergic inhibition reveals AMPA and NMDA receptor-mediated polysynaptic network-driven responses in the CAI region of the hippocampus.
suppression of gamma- aminobutyric acid inhibition reveals glutamate-receptor mediated network driven events in the isolated hippocampal CA1 region.
blocking GABAA inhibition reveals polysynaptic responses mediated by AMPA- and/or NMDARs in the CA1 area of the isolated hippocampus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the synaptic transmission in the CA1 area of hippocampal slice.
the study of the synaptic organization of the CA1 hippocampal region.
the study of the synaptic organization of the hippocampal CA1 region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isolated CA1 pyramidals are able to generate polysynaptic responses, which may be important for the generation and maintenance of the epileptogenic focus.

the pharmacologically isolated polysynaptic response is mediated by AMPA or NMDA or both, depending on the pharmacologic conditions and the concentration of Mg2+, and that this response is driven by local recurrent collateral branches of CA3 and/or CA1 pyramical cells.

the polysynaptically evoked responses in the CA 1 region of the hippocampus are mediated by NMDA receptors, and that the AMPA receptor component is not a necessary requirement for polysynaptically driven activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isolated CA1 hippocampal region is capable to generate network-driven polysynaptic responses that may play a role in the generation of epileptiform activity.
the polysynaptically evoked responses are driven by the local collateral of pyramidal cell.
the isolated hippocampal CA1 region can generate polysynaptic responses that may be relevant to network activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel polysynaptic response that can be used as a model system for the investigation of synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus.
the hippocampus is a very complex system and it is not possible to understand the function of the CA1 pyramides without taking into account the polysynaptic activity.
the hippocampus is not a passive structure, but rather a complex network that is capable of generating complex network-driven events.
